aAbout: Zoom Earth is an interactive weather map and real-time hurricane tracker by Neave Interactive. It shows near real-time satellite imagery updated every 10 minutes from NOAA GOES, JMA Himawari and EUMETSAT Meteosat geostationary satellites, HD imagery updated twice a day from NASA's Aqua and Terra satellites, rain radar with nowcasting, and forecast maps for rain, wind, temperature, pressure and more from the ICON and GFS models. It runs free on the web and in iOS and Android apps, with extra features behind Zoom Earth Pro. It is a weather and satellite tool — not a camera network, and it does not track flights or ships.
aStrengths: Zoom Earth is the cleaner, faster weather check: satellite imagery refreshed every 10 minutes, rain radar with nowcasting, a best-in-class hurricane tracker drawing on NHC, JTWC, NRL and IBTrACS data, wildfire heat spots from NASA FIRMS, and a focused set of forecast-model maps — all in an uncluttered interface that opens instantly on the web or in its well-rated mobile apps, with no account needed for basic use. If the question is 'what is the weather doing right now, from space?', Zoom Earth answers it with the least friction.
bAbout: Windy.com visualises forecast-model weather as animated map layers — wind, rain, temperature, pressure, clouds, waves and more — drawn from ECMWF, GFS, ICON and other models, with radar and satellite layers, detailed point forecasts, meteograms and airgrams, a hurricane tracker and a layer of public webcams. A free tier covers the core maps; Windy Premium unlocks higher-resolution data, longer forecast ranges and extra detail. Developer APIs are sold separately from the consumer app.
bStrengths: Windy is the deeper weather platform overall: the largest layer catalogue of the two (50+ weather layers), multiple global and regional models with ECMWF at the centre, radar and satellite blends, hurricane tracking, airgram and meteogram detail for aviation and sailing, weather alerts for favourite places, a webcam layer, and developer APIs. If weather is something you read closely or plan your life around — sailing, flying, surfing, storm-watching — Windy's depth wins.
betterAnswer: For simplicity, Zoom Earth is better: a focused satellite-and-radar map, free, with 10-minute imagery and serious hurricane tracking and almost nothing to learn. For depth, Windy is better: more layers, more models, detailed point forecasts, alerts, webcams and a community, for about $35 a year. Occasional weather-checkers and storm-watchers should start with Zoom Earth; sailors, pilots and other serious readers usually end up on Windy.

intro: Zoom Earth and Windy are both free weather maps built on satellite imagery and global forecast models — and they make opposite bets about what a weather map should be. Zoom Earth, by Neave Interactive, is the focused specialist: satellite imagery every 10 minutes, rain radar with nowcasting and a best-in-class hurricane tracker, in a clean interface with almost nothing to configure. Windy is the maximalist platform: 50+ animated layers, multiple forecast models including ECMWF, detailed point forecasts, alerts and a webcam layer. Which one suits you depends on whether you check the weather or read it.
pricingA: Zoom Earth is free for basic use on the web and in its iOS and Android apps, with no account required. Zoom Earth Pro adds more features through auto-renewable subscriptions sold via the app stores: the US App Store listing shows Pro price points of $1.99 and $11.99, but it does not label which billing period each price corresponds to, so we won't assign one — its terms say subscriptions are billed periodically, as specified at the time of purchase. No free trial of Pro was stated on the official pages checked.
pricingB: Generous free tier. Windy Premium costs about $35/year (community-confirmed pricing for 2026; sold as an auto-renewing subscription or a one-time payment for a year) and unlocks higher-resolution data, longer ranges and extra features. Windy confirms there is no free trial of Premium. Developer APIs are priced separately — the Map Forecast API's Professional tier is €990/year.

verdictA: Choose Zoom Earth if you want the weather at a glance — 10-minute satellite imagery, radar, wildfire heat spots and serious hurricane tracking — open in seconds on any device, free, with no install and almost nothing to learn.
verdictB: Choose Windy if you read weather seriously — sailing, flying, storm-watching or trip planning — and want the deepest layers, model choice, point-forecast detail, alerts and webcams in one professional platform.
verdictLine: Zoom Earth is the glance — a focused satellite and radar map that answers 'what is happening now?' in seconds. Windy is the deep read — a professional forecast platform that answers 'what happens next, in detail?' The first is free and simple; the second is deep, and cheap to unlock in full.
worldEye: WorldEye treats weather as one layer among many: its free 3D globe carries a live weather layer alongside live flights, satellites, ships, earthquakes, wildfires and 74,229 public cameras across 105 countries, with no signup. It is not a forecast-model tool and doesn't pretend to compete with either specialist on meteorological depth — its satellite cadence does not match Zoom Earth's, and its layers do not match Windy's — it's the place to see weather in context with everything else moving on the planet. An optional Pro tier ($7.99/week, $13.99/month or $74.99/year) adds the OSINT toolkit and intel feeds.
